page_title: Kopi: the open-source clipboard manager for Mac and Windows

summary.name: Kopi
summary.one_liner: Kopi is a free, open-source clipboard manager for macOS and Windows that keeps a searchable history of everything you copy, stored locally on your computer.
keywords: clipboard sync between mac and pc
use_cases: Searching for something copied earlier today or last month
Finding text in screenshots such as booking references or error messages
Saving and reusing replies, signatures, or commands via snippets
Organising clips into project or client pinboards
Syncing a clipboard history between a Mac and a Windows PC on the same network
summary.what_it_does: Kopi runs in the background and records everything copied, including text, rich text, links, images, files, colors and code. Search matches partial text as you type and can be filtered by kind or source app. It reads text from copied images and screenshots using the OS built-in text recognition, processed on the computer. Snippets store reusable text with placeholders for dates, a previous clip, or input, and pinboards let you pin clips or group them into named, colored boards. Optional end-to-end encrypted sync passes clipboard history between computers on the same network without a server.
notable: Open source under MIT license, with public code on GitHub
Searches text inside copied screenshots and images locally
Syncs history between Mac and Windows over the local network with end-to-end encryption, off by default
Skips content from password managers and concealed copies
caveats: Currently an alpha release; the Windows alpha is still in progress per the roadmap
Sync only works between computers on the same network and is off until enabled
Stable 1.0 release is planned but not yet out
